business_problem: GLS needed to unify fragmented hospital data and replace a relational approach that could not scale or model the unstructured records required for a real-time, interoperable healthcare platform.
solution_summary: GLS built the Hospital Management System Open Health Platform on MongoDB and later moved the production deployment to MongoDB Atlas on AWS so Bangkok Dusit Medical Services could exchange patient records and operational data across its hospital network. The architecture creates a single repository and interface for many kinds of hospital information, allowing patient, clinical, and business records from different systems to interoperate in real time. GLS first prototyped the platform on MongoDB after a relational rebuild failed to fit the network's varied data shapes, then adopted Atlas for production to gain managed security, monitoring, and scalability. Atlas now supports the HMS V2.2 platform and integrations with systems such as Arcus Air, while aggregation pipelines are used for analytical queries inside the database. This gave GLS a resilient healthcare data foundation that supports interoperability, regulatory control, and faster feature delivery across dozens of hospitals.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs the interoperable hospital data platform that unifies records and analytics across the BDMS network.

solution_components.name: Arcus Air
solution_components.role: Acts as one of the hospital information systems integrated with the MongoDB-backed HMS platform.

data_flow: Hospital records from different clinical and business systems are unified in the HMS platform on MongoDB Atlas, integrations such as Arcus Air exchange data through that common repository, and analytics and user applications consume the shared records in real time across the hospital network.
business_outcome: GLS improved interoperability, accelerated development, reduced IT cost, and helped more than a dozen hospitals deliver better data-driven care to millions of patients.
metrics: BDMS manages 49 hospitals and related healthcare businesses employing more than 30,000 people.
More than 15 hospitals have been transformed on the new platform.
The transformation improves care for around five million patients.
architecture_clues: The production platform moved from on-premises MongoDB to MongoDB Atlas on AWS.
Aggregation pipelines are used for analytical queries inside the database.
GLS is migrating 35 existing applications from on-premises relational databases to real-time APIs backed by Atlas.
evidence_quotes: “We needed a solution to unify the entire hospital network with a digitized information platform to get a single view of the massive and complex data set.”
“Using Opensource RDBMS was not only far too complicated but presented risk with performance issues and would not allow us to scale in the way MongoDB does.”
“When the application was ready to go into production, GLS made the simple move from MongoDB running on-premises to MongoDB Atlas.”
“To date, 15 hospitals have successfully migrated from the legacy hospital information system to Arcus Air.”
